previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with a complex medical history including chronic diastolic heart failure, interstitial lung disease, obstructive sleep apnea, asthma, type 2 diabetes, morbid obesity, and a history of venous thromboembolism was admitted for observation after undergoing a LEEP procedure for cervical dysplasia. She was monitored closely due to her comorbidities but had an uncomplicated post-operative course. Pain was controlled with acetaminophen, she advanced to a regular diet, voided spontaneously, and ambulated independently. She remained on home medications for heart and lung conditions, used CPAP, and was managed with insulin for glucose control. Prophylactic Lovenox and pneumatic boots were used for clot prevention, and warfarin was restarted before discharge. She was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to avoid vaginal activity for two weeks and to follow up with her gynecologist.
